payload.title: TCP segments
payload.summary: Validate variable TCP headers, options, flags, checksums, and wrapping sequence arithmetic without depending on native C wire layouts.

prerequisites: Big-endian integers, checked size_t arithmetic, and one's-complement checksum addition
IPv4 pseudo-headers and modular unsigned sequence-number arithmetic
outcomes: Decode fixed and variable TCP header fields, all nine flags, options, and payload spans
Build a checksummed TCP segment after a complete atomic preflight
Compare wrapping sequence numbers without implementation-defined signed conversion

payload.exercise: Fill in each lesson-specific TODO in lessons/06_tcp_segments/exercise.c without changing lesson.h.
checks: Validate data offset, reserved bits, options, payload, and pseudo-header inputs before publishing or writing
Match exact SYN and odd-payload fixtures while preserving initialized outputs on failures
Implement sequence comparison with unsigned modular subtraction and the half-range rule

allowed: In-memory TCP segment parsing, construction, checksums, and sequence arithmetic
Explicit caller-owned IPv4, options, payload, and destination spans
Pinned Linux v6.6 UAPI and implementation source as conceptual provenance
excluded: Network access, raw sockets, packet capture, or external commands
A TCP connection, handshake state, retransmission, congestion control, timers, or reassembly
Packed structures, bitfields, packet overlays, allocation, or mutable globals
